Thought: Let's analyze the proton NMR spectrum to identify the different types of chemically equivalent hydrogens:

1. δ 2.23 (s, 3H) - A singlet representing 3 equivalent hydrogens (likely a methyl group)
2. δ 2.81 (t, 2H) - A triplet representing 2 equivalent hydrogens (likely a CH2 group)
3. δ 2.98 (t, 2H) - Another triplet representing 2 different equivalent hydrogens (another CH2 group)
4. δ 7.17 (ddd, 7H) - A complex signal representing 7 equivalent aromatic hydrogens
5. δ 7.90 (ddd, 2H) - A complex signal representing 2 different equivalent aromatic hydrogens

Each of these signals represents a different chemical environment, so there are 5 different types of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms in this compound.
